subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that cos(π/11) cos(2π/11) cos(3π/11) cos(4π/11) cos(5π/11) = 1/32.

mark_split.label: Multiply and divide by 2⁵ sin θ

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 36(ii), book p.91. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The two marks sit on the step that manufactures the sine and on the closing reduction; turning the five angles into a doubling chain stays on the page as unmarked working. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1-Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, and Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations holds two of those ten slots. NUMERIC CHECK before authoring: the product was evaluated to 12 decimal places as 0.031250000000, which is exactly 1/32. Five cosines give 2⁵ = 32, and the count of doublings was checked against that. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. LINES EXPANDED 2026-09-14 (founder direction, modelled on the Maths-2A and Maths-2B expansions): every move is written on its own line, with the reason or the arithmetic shown before it is used; the steps, marks and split are unchanged.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this one — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Make a doubling chain
steps.margin_note: The five angles π/11, 2π/11, 4π/11, 8π/11, 16π/11 double each time. Two of the printed angles have to be rewritten to reach them, and each rewrite brings a minus sign.
lines: Make each angle double the one before:
[∵ cos(π − θ) = −cos θ, cos(2π − θ) = cos θ]

recall.must_convey: That cos(3π/11) = −cos(8π/11) and cos(5π/11) = −cos(16π/11), so the five angles become a doubling chain and the minus signs cancel.
accept: rewrite three pi by eleven as minus cos eight pi by eleven
five pi by eleven becomes minus cos sixteen pi by eleven
the angles become one two four eight sixteen over eleven
turn the angles into a doubling chain

steps.why: Only angles that keep doubling can be telescoped. Replacing 3π/11 by 8π/11 and 5π/11 by 16π/11 costs one minus sign each, and the two minus signs cancel.
common_mistakes: Changing only one angle and losing a minus sign.
steps.memory_tip: Aim for the chain 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 over 11. Two rewrites are needed and their minus signs cancel each other.

steps.label: Multiply and divide by 2⁵ sin θ
steps.margin_note: First mark. Count the cosines: five, so introduce 2⁵ sin θ. Each 2 pairs with the sine just made and the next cosine, doubling the angle once.
lines: L.H.S = cos θ cos 2θ cos 4θ cos 8θ cos 16θ

lines.text: Multiply and divide by 2⁵ sin θ = 32 sin θ
(2 sin θ cos θ = sin 2θ; then 2 sin 2θ cos 2θ
= sin 4θ; and so on, up to sin 32θ)

lines: [sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ, used five times]

recall.must_convey: That 2⁵ sin θ is introduced top and bottom, and sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ is applied five times to reach sin 32θ.
accept: multiply and divide by thirty two sin theta so a sine appears
each two pairs with the sine and the next cosine to double the angle
five cosines so five twos and the chain ends at sin thirty two theta
thirty two sin theta tho multiply and divide cheyyali
manufacture a sine and use the double angle five times
reject: sin thirty two theta is sin pi by eleven

steps.why: There is no sine on the left, so one is introduced by multiplying and dividing by the same quantity. Five cosines need five 2s, which is why the denominator is 2⁵ = 32.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by sin θ without also dividing by it.
Using four 2s instead of five and getting 1/16.
steps.memory_tip: One 2 per cosine. Five cosines means 2⁵ = 32, and the last angle reached is 32θ.
lines_compact: L.H.S = cos θ cos 2θ cos 4θ cos 8θ cos 16θ
[sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ, used five times]

steps.label: Reduce sin 32θ and finish
steps.margin_note: Last mark. 32π/11 is one full turn plus 10π/11, and sin(10π/11) = sin(π − π/11) = sin(π/11). That is the sine introduced at the start, so it cancels.

lines.text: (sin(2π + x) = sin x and sin(π − x) = sin x)

recall.must_convey: That sin(32π/11) reduces to sin(π/11), which cancels the introduced sine and leaves 1/32.
accept: thirty two pi by eleven is two pi plus ten pi by eleven
sin ten pi by eleven is sin pi by eleven
the sines cancel and one by thirty two is left
sines cancel ayi one by thirty two vasthundi
the answer is one by thirty two
reject: manufacture a sine and use the double angle five times

steps.why: sin(2π + x) = sin x removes the full turn, and sin(π − x) = sin x then brings 10π/11 back to π/11 — the same sine that was introduced, so it cancels.
steps.memory_tip: Take out one full turn of 2π = 22π/11, then use sin(π − θ) = sin θ.
